When rank is lower, the orthogonal projection matrix is rational by the Gram-matrix formula, and the nonzero transverse projections of integer offsets have a fixed positive norm floor. Adding the stated small ball fills the transverse directions while leaving every integer fiber unchanged.

Every target probability polytope has finitely many vertices, and the identity row is tautological. The positive uniform margins of affected rows lose less than two thirds of their least value under the displayed perturbation. Extreme rows imply all rows by support linearity.

At a nonempty complete base, group a lifted convex combination by site to recover the exact fibers. The rational orthogonal projection of integer offsets is contained in a scaled integer lattice, so the chosen transverse ball cannot add integer bases or change existing fibers.
